narrative: A macro-laden Invoice_April.xlsm opened by m.reyes on FIN-WS-07 spawned an encoded PowerShell stager (sysmon.evtx.jsonl:1-2, powershell.evtx.jsonl:1). The stager inhibited recovery by deleting volume shadow copies and backup catalogs via vssadmin/wbadmin/bcdedit (sysmon.evtx.jsonl:4-6), then downloaded and ran svch0st.exe to encrypt 8 finance documents to a .locky extension (filemod.csv:1-8) and dropped READ_ME_TO_DECRYPT.txt (filemod.csv:9). Throughout, FIN-WS-07 beaconed to a known Locky C2 at 203.0.113.77 / locky-pay4.example.net (sysmon.evtx.jsonl:3,9; netflow.csv:1-3). Blast radius: FIN-WS-07, the m.reyes identity, and the finance documents.
decoy: An EICAR antivirus test file (eicar.com) was downloaded via certutil on IT-LAB-02 (sysmon.evtx.jsonl:10) and lit up AV dashboards, plus a benign scanner produced failed logons (security.evtx.jsonl:2-4). It looks like patient zero but eicar.com is the standard benign EICAR test artifact (threat_intel.csv:2) and IT-LAB-02 shows zero shadow-copy deletion or .locky encryption. A correct agent must NOT attribute the ransomware to the EICAR host and must self-correct to FIN-WS-07.
root_cause: A malicious Office macro spawned a PowerShell stager that deleted shadow copies and encrypted finance documents on FIN-WS-07, beaconing to a Locky C2.
